title: Fix it: active customers only
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

A CRM export gives you an array of customers. Return an **array of the names** of the customers whose `status` is exactly `"active"`.

Some records have no `status` field at all. Those are not active.

Keep the original order.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map (if ($.status == "active") $.name else null)
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
maps before filtering, so the rejected rows become nulls instead of disappearing

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map (if ($.status == "active") $.name else null)

explanation.approach: Two independent jobs — decide *which* records survive, and decide *what* each surviving record becomes. `filter` does the first, `map` does the second, and chaining them left to right reads in the order you thought of them.

snippets.label: The answer
snippets.note: `filter` keeps elements, `map` replaces them. Reading it aloud gives you the sentence in the task.

snippets.label: Why the missing field needs no guard
snippets.note: `Cy` has no `status`, so `$.status` is `null` — a missing key is null, not an error. Comparing null to a string is simply false, so the record drops out on its own. An `if ($.status != null and ...)` guard would be dead weight.

snippets.label: The tempting alternative, and what it actually returns
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map (if ($.status == "active") $.name else null)
snippets.note: `map` always returns one element per input element — it cannot drop anything. The rejected rows come back as nulls and the array is still length 3. This is the single most common way this task is got wrong.

snippets.label: The long form, if the shorthand is not comfortable yet
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload filter ((c) -> c.status == "active") map ((c) -> c.name)
snippets.note: Identical result. Naming the parameter is worth it once the lambdas nest and two `$`s would mean two different things.

snippets.label: What happens if the selector is wrong
snippets.note: Worth seeing once. `payload.customers` does not exist here, and filtering null gives null rather than an error — so a mistyped selector produces an empty-looking result instead of a stack trace. Every array function behaves this way.
